title: agent-compose spec file
description: Structural schema for a single agent-compose YAML file (spec file or deploy/<target>.yml). Per-file shape only: cross-file reference resolution, exhaustiveness, cycle termination, and every other static check listed in docs/grammar.md Appendix B belong to `agent-compose validate`. Grammar: docs/grammar.md.

version.description: Spec version. Required in the entrypoint (main.yml) and in every deploy/<target>.yml; optional in imported files, where it must match the entrypoint. Must be one of the compiler build's SUPPORTED_SPEC_VERSIONS. Grammar 1.3.

imports.description: Explicit list of spec files composing this project, relative to the entrypoint's directory. No directory scanning, no globs, no transitive imports: only the entrypoint may declare this key. Grammar 1.4 / PRD 5.1.

items.description: Relative path to a spec file: `/`-separated segments, each `.`, `..`, or a name matching [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*, ending in .yml or .yaml. No leading /, no backslashes, no whitespace - one portable spelling keeps a path identical in the IR, on a command line, and in a diagnostic on every host. Grammar 1.4.

defaults.description: Project-wide node policy defaults: the third level of the retry/timeout/on_error resolution chain (flow override > node > defaults > built-in fail). At most one `defaults:` section per composition. Grammar 9.3 / PRD 5.5.

state.description: Shared graph state: one entry per channel, each a type node plus the channel-only keys `reduce` and `default`. At most one `state:` section per composition. Grammar 10 / PRD 5.7.

triggers.description: What causes an execution to exist. The entrypoints of a project are exactly the flows its triggers point at. At most one `triggers:` section per composition. Grammar 13 / PRD 5.11.

hub.description: DEPLOY FILE ONLY. The process that owns the graph: scheduler, journal, wait board and triggers. Workers dial out to it and never the other way round. Grammar 14.2 / PRD resolved q37, q38, q44.

placements.description: DEPLOY FILE ONLY. Logical names a worker claims at an authenticated join, each naming the components that claim runs. Live static grammar: every rule is checked, and the worker protocol lands with the runtime. Grammar 14.1 / PRD resolved q38.

storage_backends.description: DEPLOY FILE ONLY. Physical backing for stores: per-kind defaults plus named aliases that `store.<s>.backend` refers to. Resolution: explicit alias -> per-kind defaults -> target built-in. Grammar 14.3 / PRD 5.8.

defaults.description: Per-store-kind fallback backend, used by stores that declare no `backend:` alias.

aliases.description: Named abstract slots. A store's `backend: <alias>` resolves here for this target; an alias referenced but undefined in the active target is a compile error.

package_registry.description: DEPLOY FILE ONLY. Where a generated project's installer resolves packages from; build writes a bunfig.toml and an .npmrc from it. Grammar 14.6 / PRD resolved q59.

trace_sink.description: DEPLOY FILE ONLY. Where every settled execution's trace ships, on the same journal-backed at-least-once delivery a callback: uses. Grammar 14.5 / PRD resolved q50, q51.

event_sources.description: DEPLOY FILE ONLY. Binds the logical `source:` names used by event triggers to infrastructure. RESERVED: parsed and validated in v0, executed in M3. Grammar 14.4 / PRD 5.11.

then.description: A placement is claimed by a worker at an authenticated join, and the join token is the whole of that authentication - so a target that declares placements and no hub.join_token describes a mesh nobody can join. Declare the token, or remove the placements (grammar 14.2, Decision D130 / PRD resolved q38).

notADeployFile.description: A spec file must not carry deploy-layer sections: only the deploy layer forks per target (PRD 5.8).

deployFileOnly.description: A deploy file carries only version + hub/placements/storage_backends/package_registry/trace_sink/event_sources: no definitions, imports, state, triggers, or defaults (PRD 5.8 per-target invariant).

identifier.description: lowercase snake_case, 1-64 characters: [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. Used for definition names, node ids, channels, fields, variant tags, trigger names, and aliases. Grammar 2.1.

reservedRootName.description: The seven identifiers with a fixed meaning inside an expression. Five are CEL roots (input, state, execution, payload, and item, a map's default per-item binding); `messages` is the implicit conversation-history channel; and `output` is the selector half of `<node>.output`, on the list to keep that token to one meaning rather than because it is a root - no surface exposes a bare `output`. None of them may name a state channel or a flow-local node id: a node named `input` would make `input.output.x` ambiguous with the flow input object. Grammar 2.5 / Decisions D33, D74.

channelName.description: A state channel name: an identifier that is not one of the seven reserved names - the five CEL roots, the implicit conversation-history channel `messages`, and the node-output selector `output`. Grammar 2.5.

nodeId.description: A flow-local node id: an identifier other than the pseudo-nodes `start` and `end` and other than one of the seven reserved names of grammar 2.5. A node id is the root of `<node>.output`, which is why `output` is reserved here too: `output.output.verdict` spells the node and the selector with one word. Grammar 2.4, 2.5.

controlTarget.description: A control-transfer target: a flow-local node id, or the pseudo-node `end` (retire this branch; the instance finishes at quiescence). Never `start`. Used by `on_error.fallback` and `human.on_timeout`, which accept exactly the same targets. Grammar 2.4, 7.6.3, 9.2.

agentRef.description: A reference to an agent definition, e.g. agent.reviewer.

toolRef.description: A reference to a tool definition, e.g. tool.web_search.

flowRef.description: A reference to a flow definition, e.g. flow.review_loop.

storeRef.description: A reference to a store definition, e.g. store.docs.

providerRef.description: A reference to a provider definition, e.g. provider.anthropic.

modelRef.description: A reference to a model definition, e.g. model.smart. Agents bind models, never providers or inline settings (PRD 5.9).

toolOrFlowRef.description: An LLM-facing tool: a tool. definition, or a flow. definition used as a tool (flow-as-tool equivalence, PRD 5.1).

builtinShorthand.description: A built-in attached under its defaults: the execution's own workspace, the runtime's command bound, and a scrubbed child environment. The set is closed and grows by resolution rather than by drift - a model holding builtin.bash holds arbitrary code execution on the host running the graph. Bounds are written on a tool. definition carrying a builtin: binding, which is then attached by its address (grammar 5.5, 6.1 / PRD resolved q54).

agentTool.description: One entry of an agent's tools: list - a tool./flow. address, or a built-in shorthand (grammar 5.4, 5.5). Every entry is an address: a built-in with bounds is a tool. definition with a builtin: binding, attached here like any other tool.

mapTargetRef.description: A map dispatch target: agent., tool., or flow. Map instances are isolated per-item invocations of a component, not nodes of the enclosing flow: they take no policy from `defaults:` (Decision D73) and each runs on a fresh conversation history that is discarded when it completes, never reading or appending to the enclosing flow's `messages` (grammar 8.6 rules 10 and 13, 10.4 / Decisions D29, D105). Grammar 8.6 / PRD 5.6.

cel.description: A CEL expression. Roots in scope depend on the surface (Grammar 4.1): edge guards see the source node's output plus input/state/execution; node bindings see input/state/execution; trigger bindings see payload.

pathExpression.description: A CEL path expression: a root identifier followed by field selections and integer indexes, e.g. plan.output.tasks. No function calls - the validator must statically resolve the array schema to prove max_items bounding (Grammar 4.2 / PRD 5.6).

duration.description: A duration: <positive integer><ms|s|m|h>, single segment (e.g. 250ms, 30s, 5m, 24h). Grammar 4.4.

envRef.description: An environment reference: the whole value must be ${ENV_NAME}. Secrets and connection strings are never literals in the spec; refs survive unresolved into the IR and are checked for presence at build/serve/run (Grammar 4.3 / PRD 5.9).

interpolatedString.description: A string on one of grammar 4.3's class 2 surfaces, where ${ENV_NAME} references may be embedded in text, e.g. "https://${API_HOST}/v1": http urls and headers, the whole exec block (command, args, cwd, env values), non-secret provider keys, and non-secret deploy config. Substitution happens at process start. Use $${ for a literal ${.

envRefString.description: A class 2 string that reaches for the environment: it carries at least one unescaped ${ENV_NAME} reference, so what it says is decided at process start rather than here. It is the second arm of every closed-set provider value the compiler leaves undecided for that reason - `search_context_size: ${SEARCH_DEPTH}` is a deployment knob, not a typo - and the pattern spells "unescaped" exactly as `noEnvRefString` does (Decision D108). A closed set the curated table pins to a single value has no such arm: that value is decided by the entry's own `type`, and an ${ENV_NAME} there is `unexpected-env-ref` (grammar 12.1, 4.3 / Decision D122).

noEnvRefString.description: A string on one of the surfaces where environment references are illegal (grammar 4.3 class 3: prompts, descriptions, schemas, CEL, model and embedding model ids, trigger path/cron/timezone, content types, identifiers and references - anything the classification does not place in class 1 or 2). Nothing is interpolated here, so an unescaped ${ENV_NAME} token is an error rather than text that silently survives. Write $${ENV_NAME} for a literal ${ENV_NAME}. The pattern spells "unescaped" as an explicit alternation - at the start of the string, or after one character that is not the `$` of the `$${` escape - rather than as a lookbehind, which is outside the interoperable regex subset this schema keeps to (Decision D108).

fieldMap.description: An input-surface schema: field name -> type node, denoting a closed object whose properties are all required unless listed in `optional:`. Defaults are permitted here. Grammar 3.1.

outputFieldMap.description: A result-surface schema: field name -> type node. The result surfaces are the ones grammar 3.5 lists - agent output, tool output, flow outputs, human output, an inline exec/http node's `output` (Decision D96), and the two store schemas. Defaults are illegal here and every array must declare max_items. `{}` is legal and denotes a result with no fields. Grammar 3.5, 3.6, 3.9 / PRD 5.2, 5.6.

agentOutputFieldMap.description: An agent's result schema: as `outputFieldMap`, but it must declare at least one property - the structured output is what routing reads and what makes every edge serializable, so an empty one is a compile error. Grammar 5.1 / PRD 5.2, 5.3.

execEnvelopeFields.description: The envelope of an inline `exec:` node: fields synthesized from the child process rather than decoded from its stdout. Declaring one pins its type. Grammar 8.2 / Decision D56.

exit_code.description: The child's exit status, taken from the process (never decoded from stdout). Must be declared as { type: integer }.

stdout.description: The child's raw stdout, bound as text (never parsed). Must be declared as { type: string }.

stderr.description: The child's raw stderr, bound as text. Must be declared as { type: string }.

httpEnvelopeFields.description: The envelope of an inline `http:` node: fields synthesized from the response rather than decoded from its body. Declaring one pins its type. Grammar 8.3 / Decision D56.

status.description: The HTTP status code, taken from the response (never decoded from the body). Must be declared as { type: integer }.

body.description: The raw response text, bound as-is (never parsed). Must be declared as { type: string }.

typeNode.description: A type node in an input surface: exactly one of a scalar, enum, object, array, or discriminated union. Grammar 3.2.

outputTypeNode.description: A type node in a result surface: as `typeNode`, but `default` is illegal and arrays must declare max_items. Grammar 3.5, 3.6.

scalarConstraints.description: Scalar constraint keys are type-appropriate: string constraints on strings, numeric constraints on integer/number, none on boolean.

scalarType.description: A scalar: string, integer, number, or boolean, with optional type-appropriate constraints. Grammar 3.3.

description.description: Field documentation; surfaces to the model in structured-output schemas and to editors.

pattern.description: RE2 regular expression the string must match (no backreferences, no lookaround) - RE2 is the common denominator across the Rust validator, generated JS, and provider-side structured output.

format.description: A closed set of semantic string formats.

multiple_of.description: The value must be a multiple of this number.

default.description: Initial/fallback value. Legal on input surfaces and state channels only; a defaulted field is implicitly optional.

outputScalarType.description: A scalar in a result surface: as `scalarType` without `default` - a defaulted model output would silently manufacture routing values (PRD 5.3).

pattern.description: RE2 regular expression the string must match.

format.description: A closed set of semantic string formats.

multiple_of.description: The value must be a multiple of this number.

enumType.description: A closed set of string variants. Enum-typed fields are what edge guards route over and what exhaustiveness checking covers (PRD 5.3). `enum` implies type string; writing `type:` alongside it is an error. Grammar 3.3.

default.description: Initial value; must be one of the variants.

outputEnumType.description: An enum in a result surface: as `enumType` without `default`.

objectType.description: A nested object. Objects are closed: exactly the declared properties, no others. Nesting is explicit - a bare mapping is never a shorthand for an object. Grammar 3.4.

properties.description: Field map of this object's properties.

optional.description: Property names that are not required. Every declared property is required unless listed here.

default.description: Initial/fallback value, supplying every required property. Legal on input surfaces and state channels only; a defaulted field is implicitly optional. Grammar 3.6 / Decision D77.

outputObjectType.description: A nested object in a result surface.

properties.description: Field map of this object's properties.

optional.description: Property names that are not required.

outputResultFieldMap.description: Nested result field map (no minimum property count, unlike a top-level result surface).

arrayType.description: An array. In input surfaces `max_items` is optional. Grammar 3.5.

items.description: The element type node (may be a discriminated union).

max_items.description: Maximum element count. Required in result surfaces and on any array a map fans out over - unbounded fan-out is a compile error (PRD 5.6).

default.description: Initial/fallback value, an array of the `items:` type. Legal on input surfaces and state channels only; a defaulted field is implicitly optional. Grammar 3.6 / Decision D77.

outputArrayType.description: An array in a result surface: `max_items` is REQUIRED, so model-produced cardinality is bounded and every edge payload stays finite (PRD 5.6, 5.7).

items.description: The element type node (may be a discriminated union).

max_items.description: Maximum element count; enforced at structured-output validation so the model cannot return more.

unionType.description: A discriminated (tagged) union: the item shape a heterogeneous `map` routes over. Variants must not redeclare the discriminator field - the compiler synthesizes it as a string constant. Grammar 3.7 / PRD 5.6.

discriminator.description: Name of the tag field. A map's `route_by` must equal this name.

variants.description: Variant tag -> field map of that variant's payload. At least two variants; each route target is validated against its variant's payload only (schema narrowing).

outputUnionType.description: A discriminated union in a result surface.

variants.description: Variant tag -> field map of that variant's payload. At least two variants.

stateChannel.description: A state channel: a type node plus `reduce` (concurrency policy) and `default` (initial value). A channel without `reduce` is unreduced: writing it from a map instance or from concurrent branches is a compile error. Grammar 10 / PRD 5.6, 5.7.

channelScalar.description: A scalar channel. Only `last_wins` is a meaningful reduce policy for a scalar.

format.description: A closed set of semantic string formats.

reduce.description: Concurrency policy. `last_wins` declares that concurrent overwrite is intended.

channelObject.description: An object-typed channel. `merge` performs a shallow key-wise merge.

properties.description: Field map of this object's properties.

optional.description: Property names that are not required.

reduce.description: Concurrency policy for an object channel.

channelArray.description: An array-typed channel. `append` concatenates; map writes are index-tagged and reordered by source-item index before the join, so replay is deterministic (PRD 5.6).

reduce.description: Concurrency policy for an array channel.

policyBlock.description: Policy at a composition-wide level: the `defaults:` section (chain level 3) and a flow node's `policy:` override (level 1). Both reach nodes of flows they do not name, which has two consequences the node-level keys do not share: `on_error:` here takes `fail` or `skip` only (the `fallback` form is flow-local - Decision D103), and neither level supplies `timeout` or `retry` to a `human` node, whose wait is bounded only by `human.timeout:` (Decision D102). Grammar 9.3 / PRD 5.5.

timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on one node execution, retries included. Not applied to `human` nodes at this level or any other (Decision D102).

retry.description: Exponential-backoff retry policy, exhausted before `on_error` applies. Grammar 9.1.

compositionOnError.description: Strategy at a composition-wide level - the `defaults:` section (chain level 3) or a flow node's `policy:` (level 1): fail or skip. The `{ fallback: <node id> }` form is ILLEGAL here. A fallback target is a flow-local node id (grammar 9.2, Decision D21), while neither of these levels names a flow: `defaults:` reaches every node of every flow in the composition, and a `policy:` reaches every node of the instantiated subflow and of everything it instantiates in turn - so the id would have to resolve separately inside flows that need not declare it. "Retry, then give up" is still expressible here, since `retry` is a field of its own; a node that needs a fallback declares one on itself. Grammar 9.2, 9.3 / Decision D103.

onError.description: Strategy applied after retries are exhausted, as a node's own key: fail (default), skip, or transfer control to another node in the same flow. The fallback form is node-level only - `defaults:` and a flow node's `policy:` take `compositionOnError` instead (Decision D103). Grammar 9.2.

oneOf.description: fail: abort the execution. skip: produce no output and write nothing.
fallback: transfer control to another node in the same flow (may be `end`).

inputBindings.description: Node input bindings on the two kinds where a single unnamed value has a destination (an agent node - only when the agent is string-in - and an exec node, where it becomes stdin): field name -> CEL over input/state/execution, or a bare CEL scalar. Unbound declared fields fall back to the state channel of the same name, then to the flow input of the same name, then to the field's own `default:` if it declares one - and that name-based source must satisfy the field it lands in, a validator check because the state section may live in another file (Decision D111). Grammar 8.0 / Decisions D14, D88.

oneOf.description: Scalar binding for a string-in target.

fieldInputBindings.description: Node input bindings on a kind that names its input fields - an inline http node (whose request object is built from named fields), a function node (checked against the tool's input schema), a flow node (the subflow's declared inputs), a human node (its `human.input` field map). The scalar form is illegal here: a bare value names no destination. Grammar 8.0 / Decision D88.

mapInputBindings.description: Per-item bindings. A map dispatch is one of the three positions where a single unnamed value has a destination (D88), so both forms are legal: a field map (field name -> CEL over the item binding `item` unless renamed with `as:`, plus input/state/execution), or a bare CEL scalar binding a string-in agent's single unnamed input. The per-item index is spelled `execution.item_index`; there is no bare `item_index` root. Grammar 4.1, 8.6 rule 12 / Decisions D63, D75, D88.

oneOf.description: Scalar binding for a string-in agent target.
Per-field bindings for a target with a declared input object.

itemBindingName.description: A map's `as:` binding: an identifier that does not shadow a CEL root in scope for per-item expressions. `item` is legal - it is this binding's own default name. Grammar 2.5, 8.6 / Decision D74.

writes.description: Write remap: output field name -> state channel name. A remapped field is not also written to its same-named channel. Fixes channel collisions and cross-subgraph renames (PRD 5.7). The validator additionally requires the node's EFFECTIVE write map - remapped and name-based destinations together - to be injective, so one node never makes two unordered writes to one channel (grammar 8.0, 7.6.4 / Decision D93); that half needs the state section and so cannot be checked here.

agentDef.description: An agent: one LLM call with structured output. Grammar 5 / PRD 5.2, 5.5.

model.description: The model binding. Agents reference model.* only - no inline provider or settings overrides (PRD 5.9).

prompt.description: System instructions. Literal text: there is no interpolation, so an unescaped ${ENV} reference is an error (grammar 4.3) and dynamic content travels through the input schema instead.

output.description: REQUIRED structured output schema, declaring at least one property. Load-bearing for routing (PRD 5.3) and for making every edge serializable (PRD 5.7).

input.description: Optional input schema, declaring at least one field. Omitting it is the only way to get the string-in default (a single unnamed string bound with the scalar form at the node); `input: {}` is neither contract and is a compile error.

tools.description: LLM-discovered tools: tool.* definitions, flow.* modules used as tools, and runtime built-ins attached one name at a time with their bounds (grammar 5.4, 5.5).

stores.description: Attached stores; codegen synthesizes LLM-facing tools from each store's kind and schema (PRD 5.8).

max_tool_iterations.description: Bound on the intra-agent tool loop (default 8) - the one loop a compiled graph cannot bound with an SCC rule.

toolDef.description: A tool: one definition, two usage surfaces - attached to an agent (LLM-discovered) and invoked as a `function` node (graph-invoked). Grammar 6 / PRD 5.5.

description.description: The LLM-facing description: the selection signal when the tool is attached to an agent. REQUIRED on every binding but builtin:, where the compiler writes one and this key sharpens it.

input.description: Parameter schema; also the checked signature for `function` node use. May be {} for a no-argument tool. Illegal on a builtin: tool, whose contract is the compiler's.

output.description: Result schema. Illegal on a builtin: tool, whose contract is the compiler's.

function.description: Host-registered function implementation (escape hatch; breaks spec portability).

module.description: Hand-authored TypeScript inside this project, held to the tool's declared input/output by the type checker (grammar 6.1, Decisions D132, D133).

builtin.description: One of the built-in tools, configured. The only binding that does not fix what runs at build time: the model authors the program - a bash command, a file edit - at run time, which is the trust level exec: already extends to author-arbitrary binaries, extended to the model (grammar 6.1 / PRD resolved q54). bash is a shell session; files views, creates and edits files under the workspace.

workspace.description: The directory this built-in works inside: bash runs there, and every files path resolves inside it - resolution, not string prefix, so symlinks and .. count - and one that lands outside is refused. Omitted, the tool takes the execution's own built-in workspace, made fresh per execution and shared by every built-in that took the default. Written, it must name something: an empty workspace would bound the tool to whatever directory the runtime was started in. Interpolable (grammar 4.3 class 2).

timeout.description: builtin: bash only. How long one command may run before it is killed and a timeout result goes back to the model. This bounds one command; a node-level timeout: bounds the whole agent node (grammar 9.2).

env.description: builtin: bash only. The environment its child processes run with - exactly the exec: shape. Children run with these variables and nothing else unless inherit_env is true.

inherit_env.description: builtin: bash only. Whether its children also see this process's own environment. Defaults to false: a built-in's children run scrubbed, which is what keeps a placement's environment manifest the whole answer (PRD resolved q41, q54).

allOf.description: A builtin: tool declares no contract of its own; every other binding declares all three.
The bounds belong to a built-in.
builtin: files reads and writes through the runtime and forks nothing, so it has no child process to bound.

expectExit.description: Accepted exit statuses (default [0]). An exit outside the list is a node error subject to the retry/on_error chain; one inside it completes the node, so `expect_exit: [0, 1]` is how a command whose 1 means "no match" or "tests failed" becomes routable data. Non-empty and distinct-membered: an empty list would accept no outcome at all, making every run an error, and membership is a set test, so a repeated member changes nothing (grammar 6.1 / Decisions D84, D100).

expectStatus.description: Accepted response status codes (default: any 2xx). A status outside the list is a node error subject to the retry/on_error chain; one inside it completes the node, so `expect_status: [200, 404]` is how a 404 becomes routable data. Non-empty and distinct-membered, on the same rule `expect_exit` obeys - the two keys are one construct on two surfaces (grammar 6.1 / Decisions D84, D100).

execImpl.description: Subprocess binding. An object input is passed as environment variables; a string input is passed on stdin; stdout is decoded as JSON against `output`, or bound raw when `output` declares exactly one property and that property is string-typed - the count is over the whole property set (Decision D109), and the exception is tool-surface only, so inline exec/http nodes never take it (Decision D91). An exit status outside `expect_exit` is a node error. Grammar 6.1.

command.description: Executable name or path (argv[0]); never shell-interpreted. May embed ${ENV} references (grammar 4.3 class 2, Decision D92).

args.description: Literal argv entries: no CEL - data is passed by env vars/stdin - but ${ENV} references may be embedded (grammar 4.3 class 2, Decisions D24, D92).

env.description: Extra environment variables for the child process.

httpImpl.description: HTTP binding. Without `body`/`query` the bound input object is sent as the JSON body (body-bearing methods) or as query parameters. The response is decoded as JSON against `output`, or bound raw when `output` declares exactly one property and that property is string-typed - the count is over the whole property set (Decision D109), and the exception is tool-surface only, so inline exec/http nodes never take it (Decision D91). Grammar 6.1.

method.description: HTTP method. Required: effects are never defaulted.

headers.description: Request headers; values may embed ${ENV} references. A value is written onto the request as it stands, so `agent-compose validate` refuses one carrying any control character other than a tab: a carriage return or a newline ends this field and begins another, forging a header the composition never declared. Grammar 8.3, 12.1 / Decision D144.

query.description: Query parameters, each a CEL expression over `input` - the tool's own declared input object, the only root in scope inside a tool binding (grammar 4.1, 6.1, D65).

body.description: JSON body fields, each a CEL expression over `input` - the tool's own declared input object, the only root in scope inside a tool binding (grammar 4.1, 6.1, D65). Illegal for GET/HEAD.

functionImpl.description: Host-registered function, looked up by name at build time. Escape hatch: breaks spec portability and is flagged as such by `validate` (PRD 5.5).

name.description: Registry key of the host function.

modulePath.description: A project-relative path to a TypeScript implementation inside the project: `/`-separated segments, each `.`, `..`, or a name matching [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*, the last ending in `.ts` and never in `.d.ts` - a declaration file states types and holds no code, and the generated seam imports a bound implementation for its value, which the type checker refuses of a declaration. No leading `/`, no backslashes, no whitespace, no URLs. `validate` additionally refuses a path whose prefix climbs out of the project root and one naming a file `build` emits, neither of which a per-file schema can decide (grammar 6.1, Decision D132).

moduleImpl.description: A hand-authored TypeScript module inside this project. The scalar form is the path alone; the object form adds the environment the code may read and the packages it imports. `build` scaffolds an absent file once - typed signature, contract as a doc comment, a body that throws - and never writes it again, and `validate` refuses a binding whose file is missing (grammar 6.1, Decisions D132, D133).

env.description: The environment variables this module's code may read. Declared rather than discovered: a `process.env` read inside TypeScript is not something the compiler can walk, and the per-placement environment manifest is computed from these names (docs/distributed.md 9.1, Decision D133).

dependencies.description: npm packages this module imports, each pinned to an EXACT version. The artifact ships no lockfile, so the pin is what makes the hub's install and every worker's resolve one tree. `validate` additionally refuses a package the generated project pins at another version, and two tools pinning one package at two versions (Decision D133).

packageName.description: An npm package name: at most 214 characters of lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, optionally scoped as @scope/name, starting with none of `.`, `_` or `-`.

exactVersion.description: An exact semantic version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -prerelease and +build, each tail a dot-separated list of non-empty identifiers as semver.org 9 and 10 write them. No range operator, no wildcard, no dist-tag, and no git/file/npm/workspace specifier - each of those resolves to a different tree on a different day or a different machine, and the artifact carries no lockfile to pin it (Decision D133).

flowDef.description: A flow: a subgraph module with a declared I/O surface, interchangeable with a tool's. Grammar 7 / PRD 5.1.

description.description: Documentation; REQUIRED when the flow is used in an agent's `tools:` (the LLM needs one).

inputs.description: The module's parameter surface, in scope as `input.<field>` throughout the flow.

outputs.description: REQUIRED result surface; each field is read from the state channel of the same name, once, at quiescence - the step where no node is scheduled because every live branch has retired at `end`. Nothing is snapshotted at the moment a branch reaches `end`, so a value a still-running branch writes is included rather than raced (grammar 7.5, 7.6.3 / Decision D70). The validator additionally requires that channel to be declared and to satisfy the field - every value the channel can hold is a legal value of the field, the same requirement a name-based input read carries (grammar 7.5, 8.0, 10.3 / Decision D111); both halves need the state section and so cannot be checked here.

nodes.description: Node id -> node object. Each node carries exactly one kind key.

edges.description: Control-flow edges, including back-edges. Every SCC must carry a termination guard (PRD 5.4). Two IDENTICAL edges are an error here: the duplicate adds no transition (grammar 7.2). Grammar 7.2's rule is wider - it keys on `from`/`to`/`when` alone, so two edges differing only in a `max_iterations` are also duplicates - and `uniqueItems` cannot see that, so the validator owns the refinement (Appendix B).

contains.description: At least one edge leaving `start` must be unconditional or carry `else: true`, so an execution always has a first step instead of dying on "no viable route" before doing any work. Guarded `start` edges are legal; they just cannot be the only ones. Grammar 7.6.3 / Decision D71 (no silent dead ends).

edge.description: A control-flow edge. All edges whose guard passes fire (concurrent branches); an `else` edge fires only when no guarded sibling fired. Grammar 7.2, 7.3 / PRD 5.3.

from.description: Source node id, or the pseudo-node `start`.

to.description: Target node id, or the pseudo-node `end`.

when.description: CEL guard over the source node's output plus input/state/execution. The LLM decides the value; the compiled router decides the transition (PRD 5.3). Legal on an edge leaving `start` too, where the only roots are input/state/execution.

else.description: Marks the default edge: taken only when no guarded sibling edge from the same source was taken. At most one per source node. `true` is the only legal value - an edge with neither `when` nor `else` is already unconditional, so `else: false` would change nothing (Decision D61). The edge also requires a `when:`-guarded sibling leaving the same node: with none, nothing can suppress it, so it fires on every pass and the keyword says nothing either (grammar 7.3 / Decision D107). That half relates two items of this array through a shared `from` value, which JSON Schema cannot express, so the validator owns it (Appendix B).

max_iterations.description: Cycle bound: maximum traversals of this edge within one flow instance. Every SCC needs at least one bounded edge (PRD 5.4). Requires `when:` on the same edge: an exhausted edge is not taken whatever its guard says, so a budget on an unconditional or `else:` edge would withdraw the guarantee that exhaustiveness, the start-edge rule, the skip escape, and the cycle escape all rest on. Grammar 7.2, 7.3.1 / Decision D90.

node.description: A flow node: exactly one kind key (agent, coder, exec, http, function, flow, map, human, store) plus bindings and policy. Grammar 8 / PRD 5.5, 5.8.

agentNode.description: An LLM call with structured output. Grammar 8.1.

coderNode.description: One run of a coding-agent harness, as one node. The harness is a binding, so every other key means the same thing whichever one serves it. Grammar 8.9 / PRD resolved q57.

coder.description: The whole component: which harness runs it, what contains it, its prompt and surfaces, and the harness's own config. A coder node has no definition to carry these, so they sit in the block - the shape a `human:` node already takes (Decision D137).

harness.description: Which harness runs it. `deepagents` and `native` are RESERVED: they parse and carry into the IR, and `validate` refuses them naming this release's scope rather than answering them as a misspelling (grammar 15, Decision D136).

model.description: The registry address, exactly as an agent node spells it. Whether it resolves to a direct binding rather than a failover route is another file's fact, so `validate` decides it (Decision D141).

workspace.description: The root this run works inside. Required, and there is no default: a coder node works on a checkout somebody already has, so a defaulted root would be a bound nobody wrote. Interpolable (grammar 4.3 class 2, Decision D138).

access.description: The containment preset, mapped down to each harness's own primitive - a codex sandbox, an Agent SDK permission mode. Absent means `workspace_write` (Decision D138).

prompt.description: The run's instructions. Literal text with no templating, exactly as an agent's prompt is (Decision D13).

input.description: The declared input surface. Omitting it is how a coder node takes a single unnamed string, which the node then binds with the scalar `input:` form (grammar 5.3, Decisions D88, D137).

output.description: What the harness answers with, and what the output gate parses in full. Required, at one property or more: structured output on every node is what routing reads (PRD 5.2). This is a RESULT surface, so every array inside it declares `max_items` and `default:` is illegal (grammar 3.5, 3.6).

allow_tools.description: The harness's own tool names this run may use. What enforces the list differs per harness and this grammar states the asymmetry rather than implying equivalence: `cc` enforces it in-loop, per call, while `codex` bounds at its sandbox only (Decision D138). Written EMPTY it is refused: omitting the key is how a run takes the harness's own default set, so `[]` would be a second spelling of the widest surface there is - written by somebody who meant the narrowest (grammar 8.9).

env.description: The environment the harness and everything it forks run with: exactly the `exec:` shape, and scrubbed to these variables alone unless `inherit_env` says otherwise (grammar 4.3, Decision D139).

inherit_env.description: Whether the run also sees this process's own environment, with `env` layered over it. Absent means `false`, which is what keeps a placement's environment manifest the whole answer (Decision D139).

settings.description: Harness config, in the vendor's own vocabulary. The second open object in the logical layer: the compiler checks the keys its per-harness curated table knows and carries anything else with a warning, so an option the vendor ships tomorrow is usable the day it ships (Decision D140, amending D40).

input.description: Input bindings. The scalar form is legal exactly where `coder.input` is absent, which is the string-in default - a cross-key rule `validate` decides (Decisions D88, D137).

timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on this node, which for a coder node bounds the whole harness run (Decision D142).

execNode.description: An inline subprocess step. Prefer a tool.* with an `exec:` binding when the implementation is shared or LLM-facing. Grammar 8.2.

exec.description: Subprocess configuration plus an optional result schema.

command.description: Executable name or path (argv[0]); never shell-interpreted. May embed ${ENV} references (grammar 4.3 class 2, Decision D92).

args.description: Literal argv entries: no CEL, but ${ENV} references may be embedded (grammar 4.3 class 2, Decisions D24, D92).

output.description: Result schema (default: { exit_code: integer, stdout: string }). `exit_code`, `stdout`, and `stderr` are envelope fields bound from the child process itself, with fixed types; every other field is decoded from stdout as JSON, unconditionally - §6.1's single-string-property exception is a tool-surface rule and does not apply here, because raw stdout already has a name on this surface (Decision D91). Declaring a field is a decoding choice and never changes which outcomes are node errors - widening `expect_exit` is what does (Decision D84). This is a RESULT surface, so every array inside it must declare `max_items` and `default:` is illegal (grammar 3.5, 3.6 / Decision D96). Grammar 8.2.

input.description: Input bindings; the bound object becomes environment variables (or stdin for a scalar binding).

http.description: Request configuration plus an optional result schema.

headers.description: Request headers; values may embed ${ENV} references. A value is written onto the request as it stands, so `agent-compose validate` refuses one carrying any control character other than a tab: a carriage return or a newline ends this field and begins another, forging a header the composition never declared. Grammar 8.3, 12.1 / Decision D144.

query.description: Query parameters, each a CEL expression over the flow-scoped roots `input`, `state`, `execution` (grammar 4.1) - unlike the same key inside a tool binding, which sees only the tool's own `input`.

body.description: JSON body fields, each a CEL expression over the flow-scoped roots `input`, `state`, `execution` (grammar 4.1).

output.description: Result schema (default: { status: integer, body: string }). `status` and `body` are envelope fields bound from the response itself, with fixed types; every other field is decoded from the response body as JSON, unconditionally - §6.1's single-string-property exception is a tool-surface rule and does not apply here, because the raw response text already has a name on this surface (Decision D91). This is a RESULT surface, so every array inside it must declare `max_items` and `default:` is illegal (grammar 3.5, 3.6 / Decision D96). Grammar 8.3.

input.description: Input bindings, field-map form only: the bound object becomes the JSON body (body-bearing methods) or the query string (GET/HEAD), so it is built from named fields and may not be combined with the in-block key that would otherwise carry it.

allOf.description: Node-level `input:` and an in-block `body:` both claim the request body; declaring both leaves one of them inert, so it is an error (grammar 8.3, D66).
On GET/HEAD the bound input object becomes the query string, so node-level `input:` and an in-block `query:` both claim it; declaring both is an error (grammar 8.3, D66).

functionNode.description: Deterministic, graph-invoked use of a tool definition; arguments are checked against the tool's input schema. Grammar 8.4 / PRD 5.5.

input.description: Argument bindings, checked field-by-field against the tool's input schema. Field-map form only: a tool always declares a named input object (possibly {}).

flowNode.description: Subgraph instantiation, Terraform-module style. Subgraphs receive parent state only through explicit bindings (PRD 5.7). Grammar 8.5.

flow.description: The flow definition to instantiate. Recursion is a compile error.

input.description: Explicit input bindings, field-map form only; REQUIRED whenever the subflow declares an input field with no default. Nothing falls through a module boundary by name (PRD 5.7, Decision D68).

writes.description: Write remap over the subflow's output fields.

context.description: Conversation-history scoping: isolated (default) gives the subflow a fresh history; inherit shares the caller's (PRD 5.7). This key is a flow node's alone - a map dispatch is the other module boundary for history and its isolation is unconditional, so a map block accepts no `context:` (grammar 10.4, 8.6 rule 13 / Decisions D27, D105).

policy.description: Instantiation-site policy override: the highest level of the resolution chain, propagated into nested instantiations.

humanNode.description: Human-in-the-loop pause. Grammar is active in v0; runtime support may land in M2. Grammar 8.7 / PRD 5.5, 5.11.

human.description: What the human sees, what they return, and what happens if they do not.

input.description: Schema of what is rendered for the human.

output.description: Schema of what they return; routable like any structured output, and the contract resume payloads are validated against.

on_timeout.description: Where control goes on expiry: a flow-local node id, or `end`. The same targets `on_error.fallback` accepts. The pair is jointly optional and jointly required: `timeout` without `on_timeout` has no route, and `on_timeout` without `timeout` declares a route that can never be taken.

input.description: Input bindings for the human-facing schema, field-map form only: `human.input` is a field map, so a bare scalar names no destination.

on_error.description: Delivery-failure strategy, resolved through all four levels of the policy chain like any node's. Node-level `timeout`/`retry` are illegal on a human node - a wait is not an activity timeout and re-prompting a human is not a retry - and the exemption is the whole chain's: a human node also takes no `timeout` and no `retry` from a flow node's `policy:` or from `defaults:`, so its wait is bounded only by `human.timeout:` (grammar 8.7, 9.3 / Decisions D52, D102).

storeNode.description: Deterministic, graph-invoked store operation - the second consumption surface of a store definition. Grammar 8.8 / PRD 5.8.

store.description: The store definition to operate on.

op.description: The operation. Legal values depend on the store's kind: kv = get|set|delete|list, vector = search|upsert|delete, blob = get|put|delete|list. Each op's output schema is derived and fixed (grammar 11.4). `get` is the one op whose result may omit a field: a miss returns `found: false` and no `value`, so a `writes:` of `value` performs no write that pass and reading `<node>.output.value` fails the execution - route on `found` instead (Decision D110).

key.description: CEL key expression. Inside a map-dispatched instance a write's key must derive from the item.

value.description: Value to write. `kv set` takes a field map of CEL expressions, checked against the store's value_schema; `vector upsert` and `blob put` take a single CEL string (the text / the content). Grammar 11.4.

oneOf.description: The text (vector upsert) or content (blob put).
Field -> CEL, matching the store's value_schema (kv set).

query.description: CEL query text for a vector search.

top_k.description: Number of vector matches to return.

prefix.description: CEL key prefix for a list op.

limit.description: Maximum keys returned by a list op.

filter.description: Metadata filter for a vector search; keys are checked against metadata_schema.

metadata.description: Metadata written by a vector upsert; keys are checked against metadata_schema.

content_type.description: Content type for a blob put: a literal media type, not CEL. Env references are illegal (grammar 4.3 class 3, Decision D92).

writes.description: Write remap over the op's derived output fields.

then.description: `get`/`delete` address one key and take no other parameter. Grammar 11.4.
`kv set` takes `key` and `value` only. Grammar 11.4.
`vector upsert` takes `key`, `value`, and optional `metadata`. Grammar 11.4.
`blob put` takes `key`, `value`, and optional `content_type`. Grammar 11.4.
`list` takes an optional `prefix` and a required `limit`. Grammar 11.4.
`vector search` takes `query`, `top_k`, and an optional metadata `filter`. Grammar 11.4.
`kv set` writes a value_schema-shaped object: `value` is a field map of CEL expressions, never a bare expression.
`vector upsert` and `blob put` write one string: `value` is a CEL expression, never a field map.

mapNode.description: Fan-out over an agent-produced collection: the agent emits an array, the map dispatches over it deterministically. Grammar 8.6 / PRD 5.6.

map.description: Fan-out configuration. Bounding is mandatory: max_items on the source array plus max_concurrency here. The block accepts no `context:` key: a dispatch is the other module boundary for conversation history and its isolation is unconditional - every instance runs on a fresh history that is discarded when it completes, and the sharing opt-in is a flow node's key (grammar 8.6 rule 13, 10.4 / Decision D105).

over.description: Path expression resolving to an array schema that declares max_items. Its root node must dominate this map node - every path from `start` to the map passes through it - so the array is guaranteed to exist when the map dispatches (grammar 8.6 rule 11).

as.description: Name bound to each item in per-item bindings and traces (default `item`).

node.description: Homogeneous dispatch target. Mutually exclusive with route_by/routes.

route_by.description: Literal discriminator field name of the item union - never a CEL expression, which is what keeps exhaustiveness decidable (PRD 5.6).

routes.description: Variant tag -> route. Every variant must have a route unless `default` is present.

default.description: Catch-all route; legal only with route_by.

max_concurrency.description: REQUIRED node-wide execution bound; route-level values may only tighten it.

on_item_error.description: Per-item error strategy (default fail), governing every route whose outcome is observed - a detached route's dispatches are resolved at dispatch and have none (Decision D94). A retry carries its policy inline, in the same enum-or-single-key-object shape `on_error:` uses: a bare `retry` would be a retry with no count and no backoff, which is the unbounded loop PRD 5.6 exists to prevent, and there is nothing for it to inherit one from. Grammar 8.6 rule 10 / Decision D73.

oneOf.description: fail (default): the item's failure fails the fan-out. skip: drop the item and carry on.
Retry the item under this policy, re-executing the dispatched instance from its entry; when the retries are exhausted the item fails as `fail` does.

input.description: Per-item input bindings, homogeneous form only; without it the whole item is passed. Illegal here alongside `route_by:` - each route's bindings are narrowed to its own variant's payload, so a map-wide binding would have to type-check against every variant at once (Decision D85).

writes.description: Write remap, homogeneous form only; targets must be channels with a declared reduce policy. Illegal here alongside `route_by:` - route targets have different output schemas, so a map-wide remap would name fields only some of them declare (Decision D85).

detach.description: Fire-and-forget dispatch, homogeneous form only. Illegal here alongside `route_by:` - a discriminator-routed map declares detach per route. A detached dispatch is resolved at dispatch: the join does not wait for it and `on_item_error` never applies to it (Decision D94), it may not write reduced state, and detach + checkpointing is a v0 validation error.

then.description: A discriminator-routed map declares the three per-dispatch-target keys on its routes, never map-wide: `input:` is narrowed per variant, `writes:` names a target's own output fields, and a blanket `detach:` would silently detach sinks written to be joined. Grammar 8.6 rule 7 / Decisions D31, D85.

timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on the whole fan-out.

mapRoute.description: One destination of a discriminator-routed map. Routes may target non-compute sinks (queues, webhooks, ticketing). Grammar 8.6 / PRD 5.6.

max_concurrency.description: Per-route bound; must be <= the map's.

input.description: Per-item input bindings for this route.

writes.description: Write remap; targets must be reduced channels.

detach.description: Fire-and-forget: this route's dispatches are resolved at dispatch, so the join does not wait on them and `on_item_error` never applies to them (Decision D94); it may not write reduced state.

storeDef.description: A store: durable, attachable storage with two consumption surfaces (agent-attached tools, store-op nodes). Grammar 11 / PRD 5.8.

kind.description: Store kind. Relational/SQL is deliberately excluded; wrap a DB client in a `function` tool instead.

scope.description: Lifetime: execution (dies with the run), session (persists across executions sharing a session key), or global. Session scope requires a session-keyed trigger.

value_schema.description: Stored value shape. REQUIRED for kv; illegal for vector and blob.

metadata_schema.description: Filterable metadata shape, narrowing a vector search. Legal for vector stores only: no blob or kv op reads metadata, so the key would be inert there (grammar 11.1, Decision D113).

embed.description: Embedding configuration. REQUIRED for vector stores, illegal otherwise. Both the model id and the connection that computes the vectors are named here: the storage backend only says where they live (Decision D116).

model.description: Provider-native embedding model id (a bare string, not a model.* reference). Env references are illegal here, exactly as on a model `id:` (grammar 4.3 class 3, Decision D92): the id is part of the composition's identity, not of its environment.

provider.description: REQUIRED: the provider.* connection that computes the vectors. A storage backend never embeds - `backend:` forks per target and says where vectors live, while the embedding connection is logical-layer and does not, so one store embeds identically under every target (grammar 11.2, Decision D116). The provider must publish embedding capability, checked at this definition.

backend.description: Abstract backend alias, defined per target under storage_backends.aliases. Never provider config: physical configuration lives only in the deploy layer (PRD 5.8).

agent_access.description: Narrows the tools synthesized for agents that attach this store (default read_write).

then.description: A kv store declares `value_schema` and nothing else about shape: metadata is a vector construct (Decision D113) and embedding is vector-only.
A vector store declares `embed:` and MAY declare `metadata_schema:`; `value_schema` is kv's (grammar 11.1).
A blob store declares neither schema: `value_schema` is kv's, and no blob op reads metadata, so `metadata_schema` would be inert (grammar 11.1, Decision D113).

serverToolConfig.description: One entry of a provider's `server_tools:` — a tool the provider runs on its own side, in that provider's wire vocabulary. `type` is required and is the key the vocabulary is looked up under; every other key is the provider's and is carried verbatim (grammar 12.1 / Decision D122).

type.description: The tool's wire type, exactly as the provider takes it — versioned where the vendor versions it, e.g. `web_search_20250305`. Never an ${ENV} reference: it is what the curated table is looked up under.

anthropicServerTool.description: A server tool on an `anthropic` provider: the Messages wire's suite. A `type` the curated table names has its documented fields checked; a `type` outside the table, and a key outside the row of one inside it, are carried unchecked — the vocabulary is the vendor's, and a parameter added after this release must not be a red squiggle (grammar 12.1 / Decision D122).

name.description: The canonical name the Messages API pairs with this `type`. Required, and fixed: the service refuses a request whose two disagree.

user_location.description: An approximate location the search is biased towards.

allOf.description: One list is an allow-list and the other is a deny-list; a tool carrying both has no answer to which applies.

name.description: The canonical name the Messages API pairs with this `type`. Required, and fixed: the service refuses a request whose two disagree.

allOf.description: One list is an allow-list and the other is a deny-list; a tool carrying both has no answer to which applies.

name.description: The canonical name the Messages API pairs with this `type`. Required, and fixed: the service refuses a request whose two disagree.

openaiServerTool.description: A server tool on an `openai` provider: the Responses API's built-in suite. Declaring any moves the connection onto `POST /v1/responses` for all of its calls, which is the wire that carries them. A `type` the curated table names has its documented fields checked; a `type` outside the table, and a key outside the row of one inside it, are carried unchecked (grammar 12.1 / Decision D122).

user_location.description: An approximate location the search is biased towards.

vector_store_ids.description: The vector stores to search. Required: a file search with nothing to search is refused.

filters.description: A comparison filter over file attributes, or a compound one holding more filters. Carried verbatim: the shape is recursive, so the compiler states that the field exists rather than what is inside it.

container.description: A container id, or a request to make one.

file_ids.description: Files the new container is seeded with.

input_fidelity.description: How much of an input image the edit preserves.

providerDef.description: An inference connection: kind plus connection config. Credentials are ${ENV} references, never literals. A kind's row in grammar 12.1 is closed: beyond `kind:` and `description:`, a provider takes exactly the keys its own kind admits, and a key belonging to another kind is an error rather than ignored config (Decision D106). Grammar 12.1 / PRD 5.9.

kind.description: Provider plugin. Each kind publishes the settings schema that model `settings:` blocks are checked against, and fixes the rest of this definition's key set (grammar 12.1 / Decisions D38, D106).

base_url.description: Endpoint base URL, as an ${ENV} reference.

access_key_id.description: AWS access key id, as an ${ENV} reference.

secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key, as an ${ENV} reference.

session_token.description: AWS session token, as an ${ENV} reference.

credentials_json.description: GCP credentials JSON, as an ${ENV} reference.

headers.description: Extra request headers; values may embed ${ENV} references. A value is written onto the request as it stands - and, where a `coder:` node's `model:` carries this connection into a `cc` run, into the newline-delimited ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS - so `agent-compose validate` refuses one carrying any control character other than a tab: a carriage return or a newline ends this field and begins another, forging a header the composition never declared. Grammar 12.1 / Decisions D143, D144.

server_tools.description: Tools the provider runs on its own side, inside the model call, appended to the `tools` of every request this connection serves. Written in the provider's own wire vocabulary: `type` is the only key this compiler reads, everything else travels verbatim, and string values may embed ${ENV} references. A `type` in the compiler's curated table for the kind is checked strictly; anything else is a warning and is carried unchanged, so a server tool the vendor ships later is usable the day it ships (grammar 12.1 / Decision D122).

then.description: An `anthropic` provider takes `api_key`, `base_url`, and `headers`. `api_key` is required unless `base_url` is declared: with no `base_url` the connection reaches `https://api.anthropic.com`, where only a key authenticates, while a declared `base_url` names a gateway that injects the credential server-side (Decision D120). Every other kind's key is refused here: a plugin never reads it, so an accepted one would be a connection setting its author believes is in effect and is not. Grammar 12.1 / Decisions D106, D120.
No `base_url`, so this connection points at Anthropic's own endpoint and MUST carry `api_key` (grammar 12.1 / Decision D120).

An `openai` provider takes `api_key`, `base_url`, `headers`, and `organization`. `api_key` is required unless `base_url` is declared: with no `base_url` the connection reaches `https://api.openai.com`, where only a key authenticates, while a declared `base_url` names a gateway that injects the credential server-side (Decision D120). Grammar 12.1 / Decisions D106, D120.
No `base_url`, so this connection points at OpenAI's own endpoint and MUST carry `api_key` (grammar 12.1 / Decision D120).
An `openai_compatible` provider takes `base_url` (required), `api_key`, and `headers`. Grammar 12.1 / Decision D106.
An `azure_openai` provider takes `base_url`, `api_key`, and `api_version` (all required) plus `headers`. Grammar 12.1 / Decision D106.

A `bedrock` provider takes `region` (required) plus the AWS credential keys `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, `session_token`, and `profile`. It is reached through the AWS SDK rather than a bare endpoint, so `base_url`, `api_key`, and `headers` are not its keys. Grammar 12.1 / Decision D106.

A `vertex` provider takes `project` and `location` (both required) plus `credentials_json`. It is reached through the Google SDK rather than a bare endpoint, so `base_url`, `headers`, and the `api_key` credential form are not its keys. Grammar 12.1 / Decision D106.

modelDef.description: A model: either a direct provider binding or an ordered failover route - never both. `route:` selects the form, so the rest of the definition is checked against that form alone. Grammar 12.2 / PRD 5.9.

modelDirectForm.description: Direct binding: a provider connection plus the provider-native model id.

provider.description: The connection this model is served over.

id.description: Provider-native model id. Env references are illegal here (grammar 4.3): the id is part of the composition's identity, not of its environment.

modelRouteForm.description: Ordered fallback route. Members must be direct models (no nested routes) and capability-equivalent, so failover cannot silently break structured output. A route carries no `provider:`/`id:`/`settings:` of its own - those belong to its members.

route.description: Ordered model.* members; the first that serves the call wins, and the failover is recorded in the trace.

route_on.description: Infrastructure failure conditions that trigger failover (default [rate_limit, overloaded, timeout]). Content-based routing is out of scope - that is what graph edges are for.

modelSettings.description: Model behavior settings, validated by the compiler against the provider plugin's published schema (e.g. `thinking:` on an OpenAI provider is an error). This is the one open object in the logical layer: plugin-specific keys are accepted here. Grammar 12.2 / PRD 5.9.

seed.description: Sampling seed, where the provider supports it.

thinking.description: Extended-thinking configuration, where the provider supports it.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort, where the provider supports it.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether parallel tool calls are permitted.

trigger.description: One trigger: a (source, input binding, response mode) tuple targeting a flow. `type:` selects the shape, so the rest of the entry is checked against that shape alone. Grammar 13 / PRD 5.11.

type.description: Which invocation source this trigger declares. manual and http are active in v0; schedule and event are reserved grammar (parsed and validated, no-op).

triggerInput.description: Flow input field -> CEL over the trigger payload, compile-checked against the target flow's input schema.

manualTrigger.description: CLI/SDK invocation: `agent-compose run <flow> --input k=v`. Declares no `input:` bindings - CLI arguments are validated against the flow's input schema at run start instead. Declaring it is optional: the same CLI entry exists implicitly for every flow (grammar 13, Decision D64); writing it out documents the entry and lets it carry `description:` or a `session_key:` remap. Grammar 13.2.

session_key.description: CEL over payload producing the session identity. Defaults to "payload.session" - the CLI's `--session <key>`, the manual payload's only member - so a manual trigger always satisfies the session-coherence check statically (grammar 11.3).

httpTrigger.description: The graph as an endpoint. Generated apps expose start/resume/status routes. Grammar 13.3 / PRD 5.11.

path.description: Route path: starts with / and contains no whitespace (default /triggers/<trigger name>). Router-specific parameter syntax such as /reviews/:id is passed through unexamined. Env references are illegal: the route is part of the API surface the IR describes (grammar 4.3 class 3, Decision D92). Grammar 13.3.

method.description: HTTP method for the start route (default POST).

input.description: Bindings, CEL over payload.body / payload.query / payload.headers / payload.path / payload.method.

session_key.description: CEL over payload producing the session identity for session-scoped stores and history.

respond.description: async (default) returns an execution id immediately; sync blocks and returns the flow's outputs, and requires the flow to be statically interrupt-free.

timeout.description: Response budget for respond: sync (default 60s). On expiry the response upgrades to async (202 + execution id) and the execution continues durably. Illegal on an async trigger, which has already responded: there is no response left for a budget to bound.

callback.description: CEL over payload producing a completion webhook URL. Async only: `callback` with `respond: sync` is a compile error, since a synchronous response already returns the outputs.

auth.description: How an inbound call to this trigger is authenticated, and with it the resume and status routes of every execution it starts. Absent means all three are open. Auth is per trigger, never server-wide: who may invoke this flow is readable off the trigger that exposes it (grammar 13.3 / PRD resolved q32).

callback_auth.description: How a delivered callback identifies itself to its receiver. Opt-in, and declaring it makes callback_allow mandatory. Absent is the documented test posture: the deployment signs nothing and may POST wherever the payload said (grammar 13.3 / PRD resolved q33).

callback_allow.description: The URL patterns this trigger's callback may point at, matched against the whole callback URL with * standing for any run of characters. Required wherever callback_auth is declared (grammar 13.3 / PRD resolved q33).

then.description: A synchronous trigger returns the flow's outputs on the request itself; a completion webhook has nothing left to deliver.

else.description: `respond:` defaults to async, and an async trigger has already responded with an execution id - so `timeout:` bounds nothing observable and is an error rather than a silently inert key (grammar 13.3, Decision D81).

then.description: Both keys describe how a completion webhook is delivered, and a trigger with no `callback:` delivers none - so each is inert there and is an error rather than a silently ignored key, the posture Decision D81 takes on `timeout:` (grammar 13.3).

The callback URL comes from the request payload and is attacker-controlled by construction, so a deployment careful enough to authenticate its deliveries must not send them wherever a payload said: declaring `callback_auth:` makes `callback_allow:` mandatory (grammar 13.3, Decision D126 / PRD resolved q33).

inboundAuth.description: An http trigger's inbound `auth:` block: exactly one scheme. A request carries one credential, so verifying either would leave the route as open as its weaker half. Both secrets are ${ENV} references - a secret never lives in the spec text (grammar 13.3, 4.3 / PRD resolved q32).

bearer.description: A static secret compared, in constant time, against a named header.

hmac.description: A signature over the raw request body, compared in constant time - the GitHub-shaped family most webhook vendors speak.

bearerAuth.description: A static-token scheme, inbound or outbound: one shape and one pair of defaults, because it is the same convention in both directions (grammar 13.3).

token.description: The credential, as an ${ENV} reference. Never a literal (grammar 4.3, Decision D41).

header.description: The header the token is read from, or written to (default Authorization). One HTTP header name, in the form a provider's headers: keys take: outbound the resolved name is written onto the request as it stands, so a space, a colon or a newline in it would forge a second header; inbound it is the name a caller's header is looked up by, matched case-insensitively since HTTP/2 lowercases header names on the wire (grammar 13.3, 12.1).

prefix.description: What precedes the token in that header (default "Bearer ", trailing space included). Punctuation and spaces are the point; a control character is not, because outbound a carriage return here ends the field and begins another, and inbound it is a byte no header value a caller sent can carry (grammar 13.3).

inboundHmac.description: The inbound hmac scheme: a signature over the RAW request body, verified with the digest, encoding and prefix the calling vendor uses, and compared in constant time - an early return on the first differing byte hands a caller who can time it the expected signature (grammar 13.3 / PRD resolved q32).

secret.description: The signing key, as an ${ENV} reference. Never a literal (grammar 4.3, Decision D41).

header.description: The header the signature arrives in (default X-Signature). One HTTP header name, in the form a provider's headers: keys take, matched case-insensitively since HTTP/2 lowercases header names on the wire (grammar 13.3, 12.1).

encoding.description: How the signature is written on the wire (default hex).

prefix.description: What precedes the signature in that header, e.g. "sha256=" (default: the empty string). Punctuation is the point; a control character is not, because it is a byte no header value a caller sent can carry (grammar 13.3).

callbackAuth.description: An http trigger's outbound `callback_auth:` block: at least one scheme, and both together are legal. Some receivers verify a static token more readily than a signature, and one trigger may deliver to a receiver that wants both (grammar 13.3 / PRD resolved q33).

bearer.description: A static token on every delivery.

hmac.description: A signature over the delivered body.

callbackBearerAuth.description: The outbound bearer scheme: a bearerAuth whose header: may not be one the delivery already writes. Every delivery carries X-AgentCompose-Event, -Delivery, -Ordinal and -Timestamp, and a signed one carries -Signature - normative names a receiver is written against - and, being a POST of a JSON body to the host the allowlist admitted, it writes Content-Type, Content-Length and Host as well. A token carried under any of them replaces the value the delivery wrote or arrives joined to it: the receiver's signature check then fails on every legitimate delivery, or the delivery is refused before any receiver code runs. The namespace is matched as a prefix, the three transport names whole - X-Content-Type is the receiver's own (grammar 13.3, Decision D127).

callbackHmac.description: The outbound hmac scheme: one key, because outbound signing is not configurable. A delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256, written in hex, and carried as `X-AgentCompose-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, so one verification recipe serves every agent-compose deployment (grammar 13.3 / PRD resolved q33).

secret.description: The signing key, as an ${ENV} reference. Never a literal (grammar 4.3, Decision D41).

callbackAllow.description: URL patterns a callback may point at: absolute http or https URLs naming a host, the scheme spelled lowercase since an entry is matched as written, with * standing for any run of characters, matched against the whole callback URL. A * crosses / and ? like any other character, so one reaching the host - https://*.hooks.example.com/* - admits more than a subdomain tree. http stays legal - localhost development is the common first case. An empty list admits nothing and so refuses every delivery, which is a webhook that can never fire (grammar 13.3 / PRD resolved q33, Decision D127).

scheduleTrigger.description: RESERVED grammar: parsed and validated in v0, executed in M3. Grammar 13.4 / PRD 5.11.

cron.description: 5-field POSIX cron expression. Shape-checked at compile time, so env references are illegal (grammar 4.3 class 3, Decision D92).

timezone.description: IANA timezone name (default UTC). Shape-checked at compile time, so env references are illegal (grammar 4.3 class 3, Decision D92).

session_key.description: CEL over payload producing the session identity.

eventTrigger.description: RESERVED grammar: parsed and validated in v0, executed in M3. Backend-agnostic - `source:` is a logical name bound by the deploy layer's event_sources. Grammar 13.5 / PRD 5.11.

source.description: Logical source name, bound to infrastructure per target under event_sources.

input.description: Bindings, CEL over payload.id / payload.body / payload.attributes / payload.source.

session_key.description: CEL over payload producing the session identity.

dedupe_key.description: CEL over payload for inbound at-least-once dedupe (default payload.id).

placement.description: One named claim a worker asserts at join, and the components that claim runs. Nothing here is an address: which machine satisfies a claim is decided by whoever joins asserting it, so a placement is capability affinity rather than load assignment. Two rules this schema cannot express: placements are disjoint, and an attached tool colocates with the agent that attaches it (grammar 14.1, Decisions D128, D129 / PRD resolved q38, q40).

members.description: The components this claim runs. Non-empty, each address distinct, and each must resolve in the composition. v1 places agent.* and tool.* - the leaves that hold a machine's capability - while placing a flow.* is deferred, named (PRD resolved q44).

hub.description: The process that owns the graph. Both keys are optional on their own; join_token becomes required as soon as placements: is non-empty, which the root schema states because it is a rule about two sections (grammar 14.2, Decision D130).

join_token.description: The bearer credential a worker presents at join, as an ${ENV} reference and never a literal. Holding it is being trusted with the mesh: the whole artifact, the right to claim any placement, and the journal's effect stream (PRD resolved q38).

public_url.description: The ingress base every URL this deployment hands out derives from: an absolute http or https URL naming a host, its scheme spelled lowercase. Unlike a callback_allow entry this is the deployment's own URL rather than a pattern, so it carries no wildcard (PRD resolved q44 invariant 4).

traceSink.description: Where every settled execution's trace ships. Delivered on the journal-backed at-least-once machinery a callback: already uses: bounded retry, ordered per execution, and never blocking or failing the run it describes. There is deliberately no allowlist key: this address is operator-written config trusted like a storage backend, which is the distinction callback_allow exists for (grammar 14.5 / PRD resolved q50, q51).

url.description: The address every trace is POSTed to: an absolute http or https URL naming a host, its scheme spelled lowercase. This deployment's own collector rather than a pattern, so it carries no wildcard.

format.description: What a delivery's body is: the trace envelope itself (docs/trace.md section 2), or an OTLP/JSON ExportTraceServiceRequest hand-emitted from it. Defaults to envelope.

auth.description: How a delivery identifies itself to the sink: the outbound signing shape of grammar 13.3, because a sink delivery is a delivery and carries the same X-AgentCompose- headers. At least one scheme, and both together are legal.

packageRegistry.description: DEPLOY FILE ONLY. Where a generated project's installer resolves packages from. build writes a bunfig.toml and an .npmrc from it, both pure-generated members of the emitted file list, so a worker that materialises the artifact installs through the mirror too. A token is the NAME of an environment variable, which the installer expands at install time (grammar 14.6 / PRD resolved q59).

url.description: The registry every package resolves from: an absolute http or https URL naming a host, its scheme spelled lowercase. This deployment's own mirror rather than a pattern, so it carries no wildcard.

token.description: The credential the installer presents, as an ${ENV} reference. Omit it for a mirror that reads through without one.

scopes.description: Per-scope overrides, keyed by the npm scope written with its @ - "@corp", the scope of @corp/ui - because that is how it is emitted, into .npmrc's @corp:registry= line and Bun's [install.scopes] table.

packageRegistryScope.description: One scope's registry: the same two keys the block itself takes, under the same rules (grammar 14.6).

url.description: The registry packages in this scope resolve from: an absolute http or https URL naming a host, its scheme spelled lowercase, no wildcard.

token.description: This scope's own credential, as an ${ENV} reference.

backendCommon.description: Backend configuration keys shared by every storage provider. Connection strings and credentials are ${ENV} references, never literals.

access_key_id.description: Access key id, as an ${ENV} reference.

secret_access_key.description: Secret access key, as an ${ENV} reference.

vectorBackend.description: Vector backend for this target. Capability checks apply here: a vector store bound to a non-vector-capable provider is a compile error.

anyBackend.description: A named backend alias. Its kind is inferred from the stores that reference it, and capability-checked against the provider.

eventSource.description: Binding of a logical event source name to infrastructure. RESERVED: parsed and validated in v0, executed in M3. Grammar 14.4 / PRD 5.11.

queue_url.description: Queue URL (sqs). Not a credential and not on the closed secret-field list of grammar 4.3, so a literal is legal; ${ENV} references may be embedded.
